gauge.name: Rocky River NC near ROCKY RIVER/ ABV IRISH BUFFALO CK

impacts.statement: Major Flood Stage.  Some homes near the streamgauge site and areas around the waste treatment plan may begin to flood.

Moderate Flood Stage.  Rocky River is flooding the Intersection of Mt Pleasant Rd and NC 200 with extensive flooding of farmland and other low-lying areas along NC 200.  Floodwaters may also approach NC 200 and backwater effects will likely cause significant flooding of Parks Lafferty Rd.  Floodwaters may also approach a driveway to a care facility at the 5300 block of NC 200 and access may be restricted.
Minor Flooding continues.  Cox Mill Road, N.C. Route 200, and Mount Pleasant Road may flood.
Minor Flooding continues.  Mount Pleasant Road, N.C. Route 200, and Bonaza Drive may flood.
Minor Flooding continues. Flooding of Dutch Buffalo Creek, a tributary to the Rocky River, may cause flooding of Bowman Barrier Road between Long Run Farm Road and the Mount Pleasant City Limits.
Minor Flood Stage.  Flooding of Muddy Creek, a tributary to the Rocky River, may cause flooding of Hopewell Church Road.
Minor Flooding continues.  Stallings Road and Poplar Tent Road may be flooded.
Legacy Minor Flood Stage. Pharr Mill Road between Rocky River Road and Sequoia Hill Road may be submerged by up to 1 foot of water.  Floodwaters may approach Stallings Road and Mount Pleasant Road.
Action Stage.  Flooding along Back Creek south of Harrisburg may occur near the intersection of Robinson Church Road and Stallings Road which is near Middleton and Rocky Meadows subdivisions.
Legacy Action or Bankfull Stage.  Flooding from Back Creek may approach but not reach Pharr Mill Road due to backwater effects from Rocky River.
At this level, some low lying areas downstream around Midland, along Muddy Creek, may start to flood due to backwater effects of the Rocky River.

value.label: North American Vertical Datum of 1988
value.description: A fixed reference for elevations determined by geodetic leveling. The datum was derived from a general adjustment of the first-order terrestrial leveling nets of the United States, Canada, and Mexico. In the adjustment, only the height of the primary tidal bench mark, referenced to the International Great Lakes Datum of 1985 (IGLD 85) local mean sea level height value, at Father Point, Rimouski, Quebec, Canada was held fixed, thus providing minimum constraint. NAVD 88 and IGLD 85 are identical. However, NAVD 88 bench mark values are given in Helmert orthometric height units while IGLD 85 values are in dynamic heights. See International Great Lakes Datum of 1985, National Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, and geopotential difference. NAVD 88 should not be used as Mean Sea Level.

gauge.forecastReliability: Forecasts are not available. Only observed stages are available for this point.
